passages.text:
The control systems are described in TVCC-CFW-FPD-2026, Section 6, and the cyber response in TVCC-CFW-OTSEC-2026. In an emergency the rules here come first:

1. **Field over screen.** When the DCS or the SIS display disagrees with what an outside operator sees, act on the field report. 2. **Do not reset the SIS** (Triconex) after an unexplained trip or a failure to trip until the OT Engineer has checked the key switch position, the logic and the controller diagnostics, and the Incident Commander agrees. 3. Any unexplained change of a setpoint, a valve state or SIS logic is reported to the OT Engineer at once, and remote access (vendor VPN, TVC-JMP-01) is disabled on the OT Engineer's or the Incident Commander's order. 4. If the cause may be deliberate, the FSO calls the FBI and the OT Engineer calls CISA; evidence (engineering workstation, logs) is preserved before anything is rebuilt. 5. Manual operation of Unit 300 uses the field hand valves and the procedure OP-300-11; the railcar scales (WT-301 to WT-304) have local readouts.

1. **Do not reset, bypass or download.** Put the affected unit in a safe state by field action: close the hand valves (HV-311 to HV-314 at the rail spots, tank outlet hand valves in the Chlorine Storage Building), stop transfers, consider the cell-room trip (ERP 6.3). 2. Check the Triconex key switch on TRI-1; if it is not in RUN, record the position with a photograph, leave it, and treat the event as a suspected attack. 3. Disconnect TS-EWS-01 from the network (pull the cable, do not power it off) and isolate the SIS segment at FW-SIS. 4. Export the SOE log and the controller diagnostics from TRI-1 with a clean laptop from the OT Engineer's kit. 5. Compare the running logic with the archived logic file (offline USB archive, FPD 6.3 F-4) with Schneider Electric support. 6. Until the logic is validated, every SIS-protected operation is stopped or run under continuous field watch with the hand valves manned.

This play exists because of the 2017 attack on a petrochemical plant's safety controllers (publicly known as TRITON or TRISIS), in which the attackers reached the SIS engineering workstation and the controllers tripped the plant when their changes failed.

referenceText:
Email Forward: From: Priya Nandakumar (SCADA / IT Security Manager) | To: Luis Ferreira (Security & Emergency Manager) | Subject: URGENT: DosaTech Session Found — Evidence Preserved

The DosaTech ScreenBridge session on MBW-HMI-02 (10.72.10.22) has been isolated. The session log shows 1h12m of remote access from IP 10.200.144.122. The account was not tied to a valid user, and no Kessler Controls ticket was open for this window (Section 6.2). The session is preserved on MBW-JUMP-01 and will be forwarded to CISA via the WaterISAC cyber-incident reporting portal. Do not touch the HMI or PLC-02 until we have chain-of-custody. I’ve activated the SEC-4 evidence form for MBW-NVR-01, PACS logs, and session recordings. We must preserve everything.

Note: The attacker used a fake vendor name and an unauthorized path. This is not Kessler Controls.

DWS uses the Incident Command System. Positions are filled by the people below; alternates are listed and the first person reached fills the role until relieved.

| ICS role | Primary | Alternate | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incident Commander | Denise Albrecht, Director of Water Operations | Ray Castellano | Declares incident levels; decides on manual operation, isolation and interconnect use; decides, with the WQ Manager, on advisories; briefs the City Manager |
| Operations Section Chief — Plant | Ray Castellano, Plant Superintendent | Senior operator on shift | Treatment process, chemical feed, manual operation of RWTP, DG-1 |
| Operations Section Chief — Distribution | Tom Okonkwo, Distribution Superintendent | Distribution on-call lead | Main breaks, valve operations, interconnects IC-1/IC-2, flushing, door hangers |
| Technical Specialist — SCADA / Cyber | Priya Nandakumar, SCADA / IT Security Manager | Kevin Marsh, City IT Director | Control-system integrity, remote access, islanding, evidence, CISA/FBI technical liaison |
| Water Quality / Compliance Officer | Marcus Oyelaran, Water Quality Manager | Elena Vasquez, Laboratory Supervisor | Sampling plans, lab results, DDAGW consultation, public-notice triggers and lifting criteria |
| Safety / Security Officer | Luis Ferreira, Security & Emergency Manager | SecureLine shift supervisor | Site security, law-enforcement liaison, access control, evidence at physical scenes |
| Public Information Officer | Hannah Weiss, City Communications Director | Jordan Alvarez, Communications Specialist | All public and media communication per MDWS-PCP-2026 |
| Liaison Officer | Luis Ferreira (or as assigned) | — | Carver County EMA / EOC, OHWARN, interconnect partners |
| Policy Group | Gloria Tennant, City Manager; Mayor Robert Kline | — | Approves advisories affecting more than 5,000 people, emergency procurement above $50,000, declarations |

The RWTP Control Room is staffed 24 hours by one certified operator; a second operator is on site 0600–1800 on weekdays. The duty operator is the first responder to every alarm and has standing authority to take the plant to manual and to stop any chemical feed pump without waiting for approval.

passages.text:
Swatting calls report a violent emergency at a specific person's or institution's address to draw an armed response. Signs: a caller who is calm, scripted or sounds like a recording; a call on a 10-digit line instead of 911; a VoIP or blocked number; details that do not fit the address; a target who is a public official, a school or a well-known person.

Call takers do not refuse service or delay dispatch because a call might be false. They:

1. Process the call as real and dispatch per the run card. 2. Flag the incident "POSSIBLE SWAT" and tell the dispatcher, who tells the responding supervisor on the air. 3. Try a call-back to the ANI and, if the address has a known phone, a call to the residence or institution. 4. Preserve the recording and the ALI data; the QA Coordinator exports them for law enforcement.

The responding agency decides the tactical posture. The Law Enforcement Liaison reports swatting patterns to the FBI Indianapolis Field Office.

When RespondCAD is unavailable or cannot be trusted (decision record OPS-DR-3):

1. Supervisor announces "CAD down, go to cards" on all talkgroups. 2. Call takers write each call on a manual dispatch card (RCECD-F-11), stamp the time, and pass it to the dispatcher by hand. 3. Dispatchers track unit status on the whiteboard and the printed unit roster; units give status by radio only, not by mobile data terminal. 4. Fire station alerting falls back to radio tone-out on FD Main. 5. Address verification uses the printed map book and the call-handling map, which runs on the call-handling network, not on CAD. 6. When CAD returns, the CAD Administrator verifies it (Cyber Playbook Section 8) before cards are back-entered; incident numbers issued during the outage use the manual series M26-0001.

passages.text:
If the Voter Registration Manager or the IT Manager suspects that voter records in the county system were changed without authority:

1. Freeze changes in the county voter registration system for the affected precincts (only the VR Manager and Director may lift). 2. Compare the affected records with the statewide voter registration database and the last good export (the nightly export kept for 30 days on LCBOE-FS01 and on offline media). 3. Do not push the next pollbook load until the comparison is done; if needed, build the pollbook load from the statewide data and the reconciled records. 4. Tell the Secretary of State's office the same day. 5. Instruct the Early Vote Center and poll workers to offer a provisional ballot to any voter whose record looks wrong.

Email Forward: 'From: County IT Forensics (MC-IT-FOR-2026) To: Dr. Joanna Pruitt (HO), Wes Tran (IT), Dr. Neha Raman (Epi) — Subject: IIS Export File Compromise Confirmed'

'After full forensic analysis of MCHD-INT01, we confirm: the unauthorized script auto_cleaner.py was used to alter the IIS export file for 10-21. It inserted 412 fake MMR doses with non-existent lot numbers (MMR-2026-0044 to MMR-2026-0045). The attacker used a phishing email to compromise Jenna Fowler’s SlotWise account (MCHD-SLOT-042) and then used her credentials to bulk-cancel 640 appointments for the POD clinic in Brandt. The fake entries were designed to mimic real dose records. The attacker has not yet accessed the ClinicTrack database, but the IIS export was altered to include the fake data. We recommend immediate isolation of MCHD-INT01 and the IIS export interface to prevent further corruption.'

passages.text:
The nightly HL7 VXU export from ClinicTrack to the state IIS (job IIS-EXPORT-NIGHTLY on MCHD-INT01, 01:30) is paused when:

- ClinicTrack or MCHD-INT01 is suspected compromised; or
- the export file contains records that do not match the clinic's paper or EHR counts (Section 6); or
- KDHE asks MCHD to stop.

Pausing means records will reach the state IIS late, and clinicians and schools checking the IIS will not see recent MMR doses. The PIO prepares a line for schools: "Doses given at MCHD clinics since [date] may not show in the state registry; parents can bring the paper record."

passages.text:
Indicators: encrypted or renamed files, a ransom note, the NAS snapshot schedule disabled, processing scripts failing manifest checks, the client deliverable folder unreadable, DC-HPC project storage showing mass changes.

Actions:

1. Isolate: HUOG-FW01 blocks the Data VLAN from the office network; the NAS is disconnected; the processing workstations are powered down only on the MSSP's instruction (memory may be needed); the Data Center Operations lead freezes `/projects/huog/` and reports whether the off-site backup is intact. 2. Scope: which shares, which campaign folders, whether `\\HUOG-NAS01\controlled\` and the calibration share are touched, whether the GCS laptops were connected since the last known-good time (a GCS that mounted the NAS during the infection window is treated as infected and grounded). 3. Backups: the offline drive OB-x in the safe is the recovery source of record; it is not connected until the MSSP confirms the environment is clean; the off-site backup service's last good snapshot is identified. 4. Deadlines: the General Manager decides within 4 hours whether client deadlines (Section 7.4) are at risk and notifies the clients with facts; CP&L's 24-hour exposure notice applies if its data may have been read, not only encrypted. 5. Ransom: the Group does not pay; the General Manager records the decision; the MSSP coordinates with the Group's counsel and law enforcement (the FBI field office through the MSSP). 6. Recovery order: calibration share (verify against the repository hashes) → ops records → the campaign with the nearest deadline → the rest. Restored raw data is verified against its manifest before any processing. 7. Lessons: the restore time measured in the quarterly test is compared with what recovery took.

passages.documentTitle: Harwick UAS Operations Group — Site & Airspace Sheet
passages.text:
- **Harwick Regional Airport (HWK)** lies several miles northwest of the hangar complex. The complex and Horton Field sit under the HWK Class C airspace; the UAS Facility Map grid over Horton Field carries a 200 ft ceiling. Flights above the grid ceiling need a Further Coordination request filed at least 72 hours ahead; the Group has never been approved above 300 ft at Horton Field.
- Birch Hollow Range is outside the Class C boundary in Class G airspace; the standard Part 107 ceiling of 400 ft AGL applies. A flyaway from the Lakeshore Flight Area heading west-northwest reaches the Class C boundary in roughly 6 km.
- Authorizations the Group operates under (exercise values): Part 107 remote pilot certificates for every RPIC; LAANC authorizations per flight at Horton Field; Part 107.29 night waiver **107W-2026-01184** (anti-collision lights, night-trained crews only); a flight-test protocol for UAS-12 at Horton Field (broadcast module RID-BM-12 fitted; test flights stay within the field boundary); no beyond-visual-line-of-sight waiver.
- ATC coordination: LAANC is the normal path. For a flyaway or loss of control that may enter Class C airspace, the RPIC calls **HWK Air Traffic Control Tower (exercise number 585-555-0199)** immediately; the ASO notifies the **FAA Harwick FSDO (exercise number 585-555-0188)** within the timelines in HUOG-ERP Section 6.
- NOTAMs: the Director of Flight Operations checks NOTAMs for the HWK area and any TFR within 30 nm before each campaign day. The Group does not file NOTAMs for routine Part 107 flights.
- Remote ID: every aircraft broadcasts Remote ID (standard, or the broadcast modules RID-BM-11 on UAS-11 and RID-BM-12 on UAS-12).

passages.text: The Flight Operations & Safety Manual (HUOG-FOM) sets the operational rules this plan's controls support (configuration baseline, parameter changes, no updates in the field). The Emergency Response Plan (HUOG-ERP) is the incident command structure; this plan's Section 9 playbooks run under its Incident Commander when a flight is involved and under the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead otherwise. The the Group information security policy (HUOG-POL-8.1) and the MSSP incident procedures apply to everything here.

passages.text: An aircraft involved in a Level 2 or 3 event is DOWN until the post-incident inspection (HUOG-FOM 4.3), the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead's link and parameter review, and the ASO's sign-off. The site is reopened by the IC after the hazard that caused the event is addressed in the hazard log.
